core_axiom: Lorehold believes the past is not behind us; it is buried power waiting to be interpreted, preserved, and revived.
primary_question: Do you meet history as a rule to preserve, a ruin to explore, a witness to summon, or a relic to rebuild into action?

taxonomy.label: Founder Axiom
taxonomy.summary: Velomachus/Lorehold-style identity: the founder turns attack, memory, and archive into immediate present action.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: You do not study the past to escape the present. You study it because the right recovered truth can change the present immediately.

taxonomy.label: Order vs. Chaos
taxonomy.summary: White wants history preserved and classified; red wants to experience the dangerous, emotional truth of the find.
cards: Augusta, Dean of Order // Plargg, Dean of Chaos
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: Your reading sits between the archive and the cliff edge: preserve enough to understand it, but move close enough to feel it.

taxonomy.label: Reconstruction Loop
taxonomy.summary: Relics are not static trophies. They can be rebuilt, copied, sacrificed, and returned as tools.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: Broken does not mean finished. Lorehold asks what the ruin can become when rebuilt with purpose.

taxonomy.label: Spirit Witnesses
taxonomy.summary: The dead are witnesses, teachers, soldiers, and memory-bearers rather than generic graveyard fuel.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: The past still has a voice. Sometimes it whispers from a scroll; sometimes it stands beside you in stone and light.

taxonomy.label: Gravebreak Engine
taxonomy.summary: Lorehold often cares when cards leave the graveyard, making excavation itself the trigger.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: Your graveyard is not a tomb. It is a dig layer. Every removed piece reveals pressure, evidence, or a witness.

taxonomy.label: Archival Method
taxonomy.summary: Maps, scrolls, classifications, and campus sites turn chaotic discovery into reliable knowledge.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: The map matters because the ruins are dangerous. Method is how Lorehold keeps discovery from becoming disaster.

taxonomy.label: Reckless Discovery
taxonomy.summary: Red Lorehold is boots-on-cliffs adventure: crack the seal, chase the anecdote, and accept that truth may be messy.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: Some discoveries do not wait politely in a catalog. You may have to break the seal and run toward the dust cloud.

taxonomy.label: War Memory
taxonomy.summary: Lorehold combat is not generic aggression; it is battle doctrine, memorial force, and ancestral example.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: You fight with more than muscle. You fight with every remembered tactic, every memorialized mistake, and every story that refused to die.

taxonomy.label: Site Restoration
taxonomy.summary: Some history must be cleared, rescued, protected, or stabilized before it can teach.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: Not every ruin is ready to be opened. First secure the site; then ask what it has been trying to say.

taxonomy.label: Relic Bodies
taxonomy.summary: Lorehold often gives history a body: construct, statue, machine, sloth, angel, or artifact companion.
taxonomy.ui_panel_copy: History is not only written. Sometimes it walks, guards, attacks, and asks to be repaired.

false_positive_guardrails: Do not classify ordinary red-white aggro as Lorehold unless it carries history, relic, spirit, graveyard, or precedent signals.
Do not classify every artifact deck as Lorehold. Lorehold artifacts should read as relics, maps, monuments, dig tools, or recovered evidence.
Do not classify generic reanimation as Lorehold unless it feels like excavation, witness-calling, Spirit-statue work, or reconstruction.
Keep Lorehold distinct from Boros: less army-command justice, more archaeology, archive tension, and history made active.

ux_mapping.short_read: You do not leave the past behind. You excavate it, test it, preserve what matters, and rebuild the useful pieces into action now.
ux_mapping.maze_search_seed: ci=rw (o:artifact OR o:graveyard OR o:Spirit OR o:"exile" OR o:"return" OR o:"historic")
